text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED -> inference-queue-high-backlog (p95 latency > 2s, queue depth > 120k)
pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: service=redwood-inference-hosted severity=high escalation_policy=oncall-sre -> triggered 1710601234
alex: acked (taking primary). quick summary: autoscaler not bringing up nodes; queue keeps piling. seeing a ton of Pending pods in inference-worker pool.
mira: on my way. which cluster? prod-us-west-2?
alex: correct. cluster=prod-us-west-2, nodepool=inference-pool-gpu, target=100 -> current nodes=32, desired reported by HPA ~ 120 but cloud quotas prevent scale.
sam: logs from autoscaler:
```
I0606 15:20:21 kube-controller-manager autoscaler.go:183] scaleUp failed for nodegroup inference-pool-gpu: quotaExceeded: quota has been exceeded for resource 'GPUs'
status code: 403
```
jordan: also seeing kube events: "FailedScheduling: 0/32 nodes are available: Insufficient gpu." lots of pods stuck in Pending with reason NodeAffinity or Insufficient resources.
alex: customer impact: enterprise-tier accounts (acct: ZetaCorp, MNE-21) are seeing 429s and streaming timeouts. Routing fallback triggered for some calls -> degraded results. ops-lead, we should call this sev2 for now.
ops-lead: agreed sev2. add customer impact notes and start a post-incident ticket. assign infra-contact and cloud-suppport.
mira: attempted manual scale via cloud console -> error: "Quota exceeded for GPUs in region us-west-2". cloud support case opened: CS-48219. ETA unknown.
alex: mitigation options brainstorm:
- temporarily route low-priority traffic to CPU-backed model variants (downgrade performance but preserve availability)
- evict and restart long-running worker pods to free up pending queue slots (careful about in-flight inference)
- enable cluster-autoscaler fallback nodepool (smaller GPU type we haven't used recently) if quota allows
- implement throttling for non-critical customers (apply rate-limits)
sam: quick command outputs:
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME             REFERENCE                   TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-hpa    Deployment/inference       120%/100%   10        500       312
```
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending | wc -l -> 412
```
mira: I'll try routing policy change first. pushing a temporary policy to Redwood Router to shift free-tier and experimental clients to fallback-1 model. applying now.
alex: doing a quick manual drain of stuck pods with 0 readiness and long-running attach:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Terminated | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r kubectl delete pod -n inference --force --grace-period=0
```
mira: Router change deployed. observability: queue depth dropped from 120k -> 84k over 6m, p95 latency from 2.1s -> 1.3s. partial win.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: route-update applied by mira at 1710601500. CI/CD job id: ci-78823 :white_check_mark:
alex: manual pod deletes cleared ~40 stuck pods, queue down another 6k. still high.
jordan: we might be hitting cloud provider GPU quota per-project not per-account. we have a pending quota increase request (CS-48219) but cloud says "processing".
sam: alternative: spin up dedicated on-demand instances in a different region and route subset of traffic there. downside: cross-region latency and data locality concerns.
ops-lead: do we have a previously-configured fallback region in play? legal/compliance ok to route some traffic to us-east-1 for a short window?
alex: compliance ok for non-sensitive tenants; enterprise tenants opted-in historically, ZetaCorp is opted-in. can shift 20% of traffic to us-east-1.
mira: starting cross-region route shift (20%) -> applying weight 0.2 to us-east-1 pool.
alex: note to tracker: enable conservative cache TTLs for uncommon model variants to reduce cold-token load.
sam: started temporary rate-limit for experimental/free customers: 10 rps per org.
jordan: metrics after actions: queue depth 84k -> 57k over 12m, p95 1.3s -> 900ms. error rate dropped from 12% -> 4%.
alex: good progress, but still not recovered. next steps: continue to monitor CS-48219, consider opening a formal escalation with cloud account manager for emergency quota.
mira: i'm going to be primary for the next hour to follow up with cloud support and keep routing adjustments. alex handing off.
alex: handing over, I'll be reachable if you need help. set escalation: if we don't hit queue <10k within 45m, escalate to oncall-sre secondary and page infra lead.
mira: noted. created internal incident ticket INC-2026-1710601234 with timeline and mitigation steps.
pagerduty: User mira acknowledged the PagerDuty incident at 1710601799. Next escalation in 45m if still unack'd.
devops-bot: created cloud-support case CS-48219 and linked to INC-2026-1710601234. Support case URL: https://cloud.example/support/CS-48219
jordan: temporary manual node spin-up attempt in us-east-1 succeeded: added 12 GPU nodes to east pool. routing shift applied -> some reduction in load.
sam: measuring customer impact—ticket queue shows ~14 enterprise requests failing in last 30m (mostly retryable). add customer-facing note: incident impacting inference latency/availability; mitigations applied, engineers actively working.
ops-lead: draft sent to comms: "We're experiencing degraded inference availability due to capacity exhaustion in us-west-2. We've applied fallback routing and manual scaling; mitigation is in progress." sent to oncall-comm-channel.
alex: thanks all. mira owns until 1710604820 or until cleared. if cloud support says quota will be days, we should plan a permanent fallback flow.
mira: will update here and in INC-2026-1710601234. ping me @here if you see regression. :wave:
pagerduty: PagerDuty: escalation message queued for 1710604499 if unresolved.
incident-bot: note: keep thread for postmortem details. react with :eyes: when you read.
sam: :eyes:
jordan: :thumbsup:
alex: leaving channel but monitoring."
